title: site-claim-framework-three-voices-and-test-matrix
content:
Intent: quick, experimentable brief to ship a fresh set of hero/tagline variants + primary product page hooks for conversion tests. This is intentionally rough — meant to be a playbook for PMM, design, and web engineers to iterate.

Problem statement (user-facing):
- Engineers and platform teams need predictable, low-latency, and cost-controlled LLM inference at production scale.
- Many buyers conflate model capability with serving quality; they try to "own" models and then hit a wall on latency/cost/ops.

Primary objective:
- Validate which top-line claim drives highest engagement from core developer audiences (signup, quickstart click, pricing page visits).
- Secondary: measure enterprise interest (contact-sales clicks, demo requests).

Audience slices (for copy targeting and A/B segmentation):
1) Engineering teams building product features (mid-size startups, PLG)
   - Motivations: ship fast, predictable latency, minimize infra complexity
   - Objections: "We can host models ourselves", "hidden costs"
2) Platform/Infra teams at larger orgs
   - Motivations: SLA/backstop, observability, policy controls
   - Objections: "Security/compliance", "vendor lock-in"
3) Product/PM/Founder persona (decision makers)
   - Motivations: quick ROI, cost predictability, time-to-market
   - Objections: cost per user, integration effort

Top-level messaging pillars (single-sentence anchors):
- PERFORMANCE: "Consistent, low-latency inference built for production"
- ECONOMICS: "Control per-token cost with batching, caching and routing"
- RELIABILITY: "Graceful fallbacks and SLA-backed capacity for critical apps"
- FLEXIBILITY: "Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments"

Competitive posture (short notes — focus on what we can own):
- OpenAI/Anthropic: strong model capabilities and brand; we should not try to compete on raw model marketing. Position as "serving & economics" leader.
- Cloud managed endpoints (GCP Vertex/ML): broad infra but less inference-optimized controls and less developer UX for LLM-specific concerns. Callout: we provide opinionated knobs (batching, KV cache, quant profiles) that map to unit economics.
- Inference runtimes/self-hosted (vllm, private infra): cheaper at scale but high ops cost and brittle performance at product scale. Emphasize "predictable throughput + observability" and "enterprise-ready private option".

Hero hypothesis: test three distinct voices (A/B/C) across the top of the site and product landing pages. Each voice targets different pain priorities.
Voice A — "Engineering-first (latency & control)"
- Headline options:
  - "Ship features, not inference ops"
  - "Predictable latency for product-facing AI"
- Subheads / scaffolding:
  - "High-throughput serving, automatic batching, and production-grade fallbacks. Plug in your model, keep your SLOs."
- CTA variants: "Try hosted API", "Quickstart: 5 minute demo"
- Microcopy: small inline: "Benchmark latency by model and region"

Voice B — "Cost & economics (CFO / PM friendly)"
- Headline options:
  - "Inference that scales — without surprise bills"
  - "Control the cost of every token"
- Subheads:
  - "Smart routing, quantization recommendations, and cost-aware defaults that cut unit cost without regressing quality."
- CTA variants: "Estimate savings", "See cost controls"

Voice C — "Enterprise trust (SRE/security)"
- Headline options:
  - "Private deployments. Enterprise controls. SLA-backed uptime."
  - "Run inference where your data must stay"
- Subheads:
  - "VPC, KMS integration, audit logs, and dedicated pools for regulated workloads."
- CTA variants: "Contact sales", "Schedule security review"

Product page hooks (one-liners for three product surfaces):
- Hosted API: "Fastest path from prototype to production — simple REST, streaming, and model catalog."
- Dedicated: "Committed GPU capacity with predictable throughput and priority routing."
- Private: "Self-hosted control plane and air-gapped options for compliance-heavy customers."

Microcopy experiments (small snippets to sprinkle across pages):
- "Latency measured P50/P95 in our console"
- "Autoscale policies you can audit and override"
- "Pin model versions and rollouts without changing code"

FAQ bullets to seed product pages (short answers):
- Q: "How do you handle cost spikes?"
  A: "Automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants + cost-aware routing to avoid sudden bills."
- Q: "Can I run on-prem?"
  A: "Yes — private deployment with customer-managed network and KMS options."
- Q: "What observability do you provide?"
  A: "Per-token cost/latency breakdowns, trace hooks, and prompt-level regressions."

Measurement plan (KPIs to track per variant):
- Primary: homepage conversion rate (signup start / sessions), quickstart completion rate
- Secondary: pricing page velocity (click to pricing / session), request demo/contact-sales clicks
- Qualitative: time-in-page for technical docs, heatmap of CTA hovers, recorded session friction points

Experiment matrix (high-level):
- Audience segments: general traffic vs. developer channels vs. enterprise-getting-started list
- Variant A vs B vs C (three hero voices) x CTA (self-serve vs contact-sales) x microcopy (cost vs latency emphasis)
- Minimum detectable lift target: 8–12% uplift on primary KPI for a variant to be promoted

Implementation notes for web/ops:
- Keep each hero test to a single content swap + 1 CTA to reduce noise.
- Ensure analytics funnels are mapped: hero variant → quickstart → API key issue → first API call.
- Tag sessions by traffic source for cohort analysis (docs, blog, pricing, ad).

Risks & open questions (things to resolve before wide rollout):
- Are we ready to show live latency numbers on the homepage? If not, use indicative ranges and link to technical benchmarks.
- Do Legal / Security need review for "SLA-backed" claims? Flag legal review ticket.
- Pricing transparency: cost-savings claims must be backed by model and workload assumptions; coordinate with product economics.

Near-term next steps (2-week sprint):
1) Copy lock: finalize 3 hero variants and 6 CTA permutations (owner: PMM) — due EOD week 1
2) Build variants in Next site + wiring to analytics (engineer + web infra) — due mid week 2
3) Run internal QA and legal check on any SLA / cost claims — due end week 2
4) Soft-launch to 10% traffic; collect 7-day signal, then iterate (owner: growth)

Low-fidelity sample hero for A (engineering):
Headline: "Predictable latency for product-facing AI"
Subhead: "High-throughput serving, smart batching, and automatic fallbacks so your feature stays fast under load."
Primary CTA: "Try the API — 5 min quickstart"
Secondary CTA: "See latency benchmarks"

Notes to designers: keep hero section compact — include a small status band for P95 examples or toggled benchmark modal. Avoid heavy visual claims (no giant dollar numbers) unless product economics team signs off.

Open research asks (qualitative to support iteration):
- Capture 6 developer interviews focused on "owns model vs serves model" decision logic — synthesis due week 3
- Pull 3 anomaly cases where customers tried self-hosting and failed due to ops costs — anonymized case studies for docs

Tiny checklist for launch:
- [ ] Copy locked (3 variants)
- [ ] Visual comps for each variant (mobile + desktop)
- [ ] Analytics funnels instrumented
- [ ] Legal signoff on claims
- [ ] QA + accessibility pass

This doc is a working brief; keep edits light and track versions in the linked jira ticket. Add test results back into the ticket as they come in.

Unresolved phrasing ideas (brain dump):
- "Serve, don't stitch" — playful but unclear
- "Inference as a predictable runtime" — maybe too dry
- "Ship AI features, not infrastructure" — close to a keeper, workshop tone

If this lands well, follow-up doc: detailed product page copy + templated component library for hero, features, benchmarks, and enterprise band.
